While it is possible to use the Publish tab to set clip fields based on worker variables and regular expressions applied to the file path can be awkward when the file naming conventions become more complex. A new and more powerful metadata extraction mechanism has been added which involves providing an external mapping file that lists patterns to look for and then which metadata fields to set when importing a file if those patterns are found in the file path. You can specify a file containing metadata extraction rules on the Options tab of the worker config. The format of the file is lines of the form: *pattern*  **tab** *field id* **tab** *value to set*  **newline**. You might have the following metadata extraction rules and user field 1 would be set to “Football” and user field 2 to “Season 2” when the file above is imported. If the pattern starts with lower case ‘m’ or ‘n’ and followed by a punctuation character such as comma, semicolon or slash then it is taken to be a regular expression that applies to the entire file path or just the file name respectively, and the specified character is the delimiter at the end of the regular expression (as you might want to use something other than / when matching file paths). You can use a more complex pattern like m,/([^/]+)/[^/]+$, to extract the parent folder into $1, using comma as the regex delimiter and where forward slash is the file path separator on Mac OS X and Unix. To simplify working with a mix of Mac and Windows paths all file path separators are converted from backslashes to Unix-style forward slashes so regular expressions should only check for /, even on Windows.

results.content: * truffleHog – Searches Through Git Repositories For High Entropy Strings And Secrets, Digging Deep Into Commit History. # truffleHog – Searches Through Git Repositories For High Entropy Strings And Secrets, Digging Deep Into Commit History. Searches through git repositories for secrets, digging deep into commit history and branches. truffleHog previously functioned by running entropy checks on git diffs. This functionality still exists, but high signal regex checks have been added, and the ability to suppress entropy checking has also been added. With the `--include_paths` and `--exclude_paths` options, it is also possible to limit scanning to a subset of objects in the Git history by defining regular expressions (one per line) in a file to match the targeted object paths. # regexes must match the entire path, but can use python's regex syntax for. trufflehog --include_paths include-patterns.txt --exclude_paths exclude-patterns.txt file://path/to/my/repo.git. Additional usage information is provided when calling `trufflehog` with the `-h` or `--help` options. Custom regexes can be added with the following flag `--rules /path/to/rules`. Things like subdomain enumeration, s3 bucket detection, and other useful regexes highly custom to the situation can be added. Things like Azure keys, Twilio keys, Google Compute keys, are welcome, provided a high signal regex can be constructed. To explicitly allow particular secrets (e.g. self-signed keys used only for local testing) you can provide an allow list `--allow /path/to/allow` in the following format:. This module will go through the entire commit history of each branch, and check each diff from each commit, and check for secrets. This is both by regex and by entropy. usage: trufflehog [-h] [--json] [--regex] [--rules RULES] [--allow ALLOW]. --regex Enable high signal regex checks. --rules RULES Ignore default regexes and source from json list file. --allow ALLOW Explicitly allow regexes from json list file. one of which must match a Git object path in order for. results.content:
Title: Dynamic config (path-filtering + continuation wf) vs Script detecting file changes - Build Environment - CircleCI Discuss
# Dynamic config (path-filtering + continuation wf) vs Script detecting file changes. I am working on a single application repo which pipeline should publish only specific NPM packages based on file changes of the repo. Most of the workflow would stay the same, but let’s say two jobs (build and deploy) should change behavior based on which files have changed `current PR vs the main branch`. In the past years, as far as I understood ppl used custom scripts to get which files were changing, then read from a file what was changed and let the command or circleci config behave accordingly. @lerna/changed - npm is an example. This approach, just feels a bit overkilling having to introduce a `setup` workflows and those orbs, when all I need is to know which files have changed. A simple script such as lerna would work great for me. Am I not seeing the benefits dynamic config would bring me in close or long run ? But CircleCI’s dynamic config with their `path-filtering` orb will probably be simpler and more declarative. Here’s what your `.circleci/config.yml` could be like. packages/foo/.* run-foo true. packages/bar/.* run-bar true. packages/baz/.* run-baz true`. The `mapping` value has regexes for the changed files. So if `packages/foo/package.json` changed, `run-foo` would be `true`. Then, `.circleci/continue_config.yml` would accept the mapping values as parameters:. condition: << pipeline.parameters.run-foo >>. condition: << pipeline.parameters.run-baz >>. condition: << pipeline.parameters.run-bar >>. Here’s that code in a repo: circle-advanced-setup-workflow/config.yml at example/node-modules · getlocalci/circle-advanced-setup-workflow · GitHub.
